issues.description: Method return type mismatch for Animal.messageOnFeed(): The problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies an abstract method messageOnFeed() that returns a String and that feedAllAnimals() should print that String. In the solution repository, Animal.java declares the abstract method as returning FeedResponse (public abstract FeedResponse messageOnFeed();). Additionally, Goat.java in the solution implements messageOnFeed() with a String return type, which conflicts with Animal.java's FeedResponse return type and causes a compilation error. This inconsistency between the specification and the reference implementation (and the internal inconsistency in the solution) will confuse students and prevent the code from compiling as provided.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the return type of Animal.messageOnFeed() consistent across all artifacts. Two viable fixes:
1) Match the problem statement/UML: change Animal.messageOnFeed() to return String, update Animal.java to declare public abstract String messageOnFeed(); and update Pig/Seal/Goat to return String values (remove or adapt the FeedResponse class usage). Update any code that expects FeedResponse to use the String return value instead. OR
2) Adopt the FeedResponse type as canonical: update the problem statement and UML to document that messageOnFeed() returns FeedResponse, and update Goat.java to return FeedResponse (e.g., new FeedResponse("Maah!", true)). Ensure templates, tests, and examples are updated to treat messageOnFeed() as returning FeedResponse (e.g., print feedResponse.toString() where a text is expected). Apply one consistent choice across the specification, template, reference solution, and tests so students have a single clear contract to implement.
